title: Why students with disabilities face a digital and remedial learning gap

blurb: Forty-five countries have jointly released an international framework for vocational education. The framework is intended to guide how countries approach skills-oriented education and training, with relevance for school-level vocational programmes.

title: ‘Title I for rich kids’ and other predictions for the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit
blurb: A Brookings commentary by Jon Valant offers predictions about the United States' Federal Scholarship Tax Credit. The author expects the programme to favour wealthier families and anticipates implementation challenges. The piece adds to the international debate on school funding and choice.

title: FactCheck: Do Irish primary school teachers have the most teaching hours in the world?
blurb: A fact-check examines a claim that Irish primary school teachers have the most teaching hours in the world, using OECD data on teachers' working time. It illustrates how international comparisons can inform national discussions about the teaching profession.

title: Four-day-a-week schooling: Parents hope for wider implementation, schools anxiously await guidance.
blurb: The report covers discussion in Vietnam around a four-day school week. Parents are hopeful about wider implementation while schools await further official guidance on how the arrangement would work.

blurb: A Press Information Bureau feature describes the legal framework strengthened to safeguard public examinations against paper leaks. It outlines the Union government's measures to keep examinations fair and secure for candidates.

title: Minister Hoang Minh Son: "Education and training programs need to change in both content and objectives in the AI ​​era."
blurb: Vietnam's education minister says that education and training programmes need to change in both content and objectives in the era of artificial intelligence. The remarks point to a national policy direction on preparing curricula for AI.

blurb: According to the headline, an education minister has said teachers need to build AI and technology skills to keep pace with their students. The item points to growing attention to teacher digital capability; further detail was not available in the summary.

blurb: Ukraine's Education Minister told parliament that 42% of schools can continue classes in shelters during air raid alerts, while 82% of schoolchildren and kindergarten pupils have access to shelters. blurb: A Brookings analysis presents data on trends in American schools and how they compare with schools in other countries, offering a benchmark for where the US stands globally.

source: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute

blurb: According to the headline, Kamal Hachoumi has taken on the school dropout challenge in Morocco as Minister Delegate. The item points to government attention on keeping learners in school; further detail was not available in the summary, so readers may wish to consult the full article.

blurb: The Ministry of Women and Child Development has launched the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026, a nationwide nutrition campaign. It focuses on dietary diversity, adequate protein intake and fresh hot cooked meals, which support the health and learning readiness of young children.

blurb: The Department of School Education and Literacy has asked nodal officers at different levels to ensure accurate and timely verification of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme. blurb: Reporting from Ukraine indicates that 42 per cent of schools can hold classes during air raid alerts. The article also looks at how many institutions have shelters and generators, highlighting the facilities needed to keep learning going.

blurb: According to the headline, artificial intelligence is beginning to reach African schools. blurb: The Central Information Commission has recommended that CBSE conduct surprise inspections of affiliated schools to identify alleged dummy admissions and verify compliance with mandatory attendance. blurb: UNESCO and its partners are supporting media literacy books for children to help them recognise misinformation. The initiative aims to build critical thinking skills among young readers.

blurb: The Centre has amended the Census Rules, 1990, so that states and Union territories can appoint teachers of aided or unaided private bodies as enumerators during the ongoing census. The notification from the Registrar General of India widens the pool of staff who may be deployed for census duties.

blurb: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment notified Aadhaar verification rules for the PM CARES for Children scholarship, covering Classes 1 to 12. Children cannot be denied benefits solely because authentication fails or they lack Aadhaar, subject to alternative verification procedures.

title: Smart classrooms roll out, revolutionising learning in public schools
blurb: Kenya is rolling out smart boards and teacher laptops to public junior schools under the National Digital Class Experience, supporting the Competency-Based Education curriculum. title: Centre expands Census enumerator pool to include private school teachers, clerks
blurb: The Centre has widened the pool of people who can serve as Census enumerators to include private school teachers and clerks.

blurb: A study reports that Australian primary students are taught basic maths two years later than peers in other countries. The comparison offers cross-country evidence on when foundational numeracy is introduced in primary school.

blurb: UNESCO highlights how an initiative called Karishma from India is using AI and digital channels to widen access to sexuality education.

blurb: This article from The Borgen Project looks at education in Indian languages and its link to economic opportunity. The item came without a summary, so the discussion is only indicated by its title. It appears to explore how learning in familiar languages may widen access to opportunity.

title: Only 42% of schools in Ukraine can continue classes during air raid alerts - Ministry of Education and Science
blurb: Ukraine's Ministry of Education and Science reports that only 42 percent of schools can continue classes during air raid alerts.

title: 21,000 junior schools targeted for nationwide digital learning drive
blurb: Kenya is expanding digital learning in public junior schools, with 10,382 institutions equipped with interactive smart boards and teacher laptops. ICT Authority Board Chairperson Lily Ngok presided over the launch at Kericho Township Primary and Junior School, urging teachers to use the devices. The World Bank-supported effort aims to bridge the digital divide.

title: CIC flags alleged dummy admissions, recommends surprise checks at CBSE-affiliated schools
blurb: The Central Information Commission has recommended surprise inspections of CBSE-affiliated schools to check alleged dummy admissions and ensure compliance with mandatory attendance rules. The recommendation is aimed at strengthening checks and balances in school affiliation compliance.

blurb: This ORF commentary asks what it means for a school to be future-ready, going beyond smart classrooms, digital platforms and coding offerings. title: Closing India’s foundational literacy gap | Hindustan Times
blurb: The Hindustan Times article discusses India's foundational literacy gap and what is needed to close it. It adds to ongoing national conversation on building strong early reading skills, a priority within the foundational learning agenda.

title: Nearly half of all students enrolled in IIT Madras’ school outreach initiative are girls
blurb: Nearly half of the students enrolled in IIT Madras's School Connect outreach initiative are girls. The institute aims to expand the initiative to 25,000 schools across the country in the coming years, building on its existing network of 6,406 partner schools.

title: Centre pushes open schooling via NIOS to achieve 100% enrolment by 2030
blurb: The Centre is promoting open schooling through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) as one route towards the goal of 100% enrolment by 2030. The step aims to widen flexible pathways for learners to continue their school education.

title: UDISE+ report shows rise in teachers, fall in school dropout rates
blurb: The Ministry of Education released the UDISE+ 2025-26 report, which records teacher numbers rising to 1,02,73,020 from 94,83,294 in 2022-23. Pupil-teacher ratios are reported at 10 at the foundational level and 21 at the secondary level, within the NEP-recommended 30:1. Dropout rates also declined, including at the preparatory level (2.3 to 1.8 per cent) and secondary level (8.2 to 7 per cent).

title: A New Chapter in Compulsory Education, Starting from Early Childhood Education
blurb: Indonesia is opening a new chapter in compulsory education that begins with early childhood education. The article covers a national reform that extends the starting point of the education system to the early years.

title: Learning at the Speed of AI: Using Platform Trials to Test AI Innovation
blurb: This Center for Global Development publication looks at how platform trials could be used to test AI innovations more quickly and rigorously. It is relevant for education stakeholders interested in evidence-based approaches to new technology. Further details were not available in the item summary.

title: Government allocates Rs 6.54 billion to upgrade infrastructure at 109 community schools
blurb: Nepal's government has allocated Rs 6.54 billion to upgrade infrastructure at 109 community schools.

title: Who inspects and monitors fee-based educational activities in schools?
blurb: Vietnam's Ministry of Education and Training has issued Circular No. 85/2026, effective November 15, 2026, regulating enhanced education activities and needs-based education activities in general education institutions. Enhanced activities may not charge fees, while needs-based activities can charge on voluntary registration; the article looks at who inspects and monitors them.

title: From assessment to the classroom: using data to improve learning in the Dominican Republic
blurb: UNESCO describes how assessment data is being used to improve learning in the Dominican Republic. The item gave no further detail, but its title points to links between assessment results and classroom practice, an approach relevant to learning-outcome improvement elsewhere.

blurb: NCERT's Department of Curriculum Studies and Development, with RIE Bhubaneswar, concluded a three-day capacity building programme on NEP 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. It brought together 51 nodal principals and school leaders from across eastern India. The programme supports school-level implementation of NEP and NCF-SE.

title: Google extends AI teacher training to Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Sikkim
blurb: Google is expanding its AI training programme for educators through new partnerships with the governments of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Sikkim and the Union Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. More than 80,000 educators have completed the free, self-paced training since May 2026, which covers AI tools for lesson planning and learning materials.

title: DigiLocker, ePathshala to UMANG: Top 5 Must-Have Government Apps For Students in India
blurb: The article lists five government apps useful to students in India, including DigiLocker, ePathshala and UMANG. It describes how these free apps help students reach learning materials, manage important documents and use government services without visiting several offices or websites.

blurb: This op-ed argues that reading and writing should remain central to schooling alongside the growing use of digital tools and AI. blurb: This explainer describes Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan as the Government of India's flagship integrated school-education scheme, covering the continuum from pre-school to Class XII. title: Three-Day Capacity Building Programme for Nodal School Principals and School Leaders on NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023 Concludes at RIE Bhubaneswar
blurb: A three-day capacity building programme for nodal school principals and school leaders on NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023 has concluded at RIE Bhubaneswar. The programme supports school leadership in taking forward the national policy and curriculum framework.

blurb: The Ministry of Education held an orientation-cum-review workshop on the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS). The workshop focused on strengthening how the scholarship is implemented and how applications are verified.

blurb: Education International discusses Japan's PISA 2025 results, which confirm the strength and relative equity of its public education system. Education unions call for investment in public education and attention to student and teacher well-being.

blurb: Bangladesh's ministry has indicated that MPO-listed teachers and staff at private institutions will also receive the new national pay structure, with higher basic salaries and allowances. blurb: Cameroon's Basic Education Minister has prohibited kindergarten and primary pupils from using artificial intelligence tools to complete assignments. The step is aimed at protecting foundational learning in the early years.

blurb: This commentary reviews Kazakhstan's PISA 2025 reading results, which show an average score of 385 compared with the OECD average of 461. blurb: The Prime Minister highlighted the strong contribution of teachers on Teachers' Day.

The piece notes 274 IB World schools and more than 800 Cambridge schools in India, nearly half of the latter in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, and links this to families' aspirations for global exposure.

title: How to fix foundational learning for Nigerian girls
blurb: According to the headline, this piece looks at how to improve foundational learning for girls in Nigeria. The topic relates to early-grade reading and numeracy and to girls' education; the summary did not include further detail, so readers may wish to consult the full article.

title: India's primary education crisis: Children are in schools but are they desirably learning ?
blurb: The article discusses a concern raised by Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata about the foundations of primary education in India. The author asks whether children acquiring essential competencies in early years is a precondition for excellence in later schooling and skills, and reflects on the gap between enrolment and learning.

title: RTE Students Cannot Demand Automatic Transfer From One Private Unaided School To Another Upon Closure:...
blurb: A court ruling reported by Verdictum states that students admitted under the Right to Education Act cannot demand automatic transfer from one private unaided school to another when the first school closes. The item provides no further detail on the case or the conditions discussed.

title: Turkiyya ta yi zarra a Shirin Ƙimar Dalibai na Duniya (PISA) 2025 a tsakanin ƙasashen OECD
blurb: According to OECD results for PISA 2025, Turkey recorded notable progress among OECD members in mathematics, reading and science. The assessment covered 15-year-old students across 91 countries and economies, and in Turkey it was conducted online in 203 schools across 56 provinces.

title: Only 59 Rural Indian Girls Complete Higher Secondary Education For Every 100 Boys: UNESCO
blurb: A UNESCO report highlights differences in upper-secondary completion across India, with a gender parity index of 0.59 in rural areas compared with 1.00 in urban areas and 0.89 nationally. The findings offer useful evidence on where continued effort can help more rural girls complete higher secondary education.

title: W’Bank: Debt interest eats into health, education budgets across Africa
blurb: In its October 2026 Africa Economic Update, the World Bank notes that nearly 80 per cent of sub-Saharan African countries spend more on public debt interest than on healthcare, education or both. Interest payments averaged between 2.9 and 3.2 per cent of GDP from 2023 to 2026, leaving less room in budgets for essential services.

title: AI in the classroom needs teachers in the driver’s seat, global study finds
blurb: A global study finds that AI in the classroom works best when teachers lead its use. The finding underlines the central role of educators as schools around the world consider how to bring AI into teaching.

title: CBSE’s Digital Evaluation System Overlooks Teachers And Students: Apar Gupta
blurb: Lawyer Apar Gupta discussed CBSE's On-Screen Marking system for Class 10 and 12 answer scripts. He said digitisation should be judged by its benefit to learning and raised points on planning, cybersecurity, accessibility and grievance redressal. The article reports his views without any official response.

title: Principals, Teachers From 24 Schools Discuss Inclusive Education, Teacher Training And Classroom Innovation At
blurb: A two-day Principals and Teachers Conference concluded at the Regional Institute of Education, Bhopal, bringing together educators from 24 schools. Experts discussed inclusive education, 21st-century classroom skills and educational innovations, while participants shared best practices and officials emphasised stronger collaboration between schools and teacher training institutions.

title: End Child Marriage, Invest in Girls. Protect their Futures: UNICEF Afghanistan on International Day of the Girl
blurb: On International Day of the Girl, UNICEF Afghanistan called for action to end child marriage and invest in girls. The statement notes that child marriage disrupts education and cites survey findings on early marriage in the country.

title: Literacy for All
blurb: The Press Information Bureau has published a note titled 'Literacy for All'; the available text does not include its details.

title: World Bank: Debt interest swallows health, education budgets in 80% of African countries
blurb: A World Bank analysis finds that interest payments on public debt exceed government spending on health and/or education in nearly four-fifths of sub-Saharan African countries. High debt-servicing costs are constraining public finances in the region, which is relevant context for how much funding is available for education systems.

title: NCERT Announces Online Diploma Course In Science Teaching: Registration From October 12
blurb: NCERT has announced an online diploma course in science teaching, with registration starting October 12. The source gave no further detail on eligibility or content. The course is aimed at supporting teachers in building their science teaching skills.

title: Education ministry holds nationwide screening on inclusive education for children with special needs
blurb: The Ministry of Education held a nationwide screening of a 30-minute orientation module on inclusive education for children with special needs, through the PRASHAST portal. The module is available in 12 Indian languages and supports a whole-school approach to inclusion.

title: NCERT releases most revised textbooks up to Class 9
blurb: NCERT has released the most revised textbooks for classes up to Class 9.

title: They still call us ‘jungli’. For Adivasi kids, free school comes at a cost
blurb: The article looks at the experiences of Adivasi children in accessing free schooling and the costs families can still face.

title: From India to France: Why are Gen Z students angry?
blurb: This article compares the School Thik Karo campaign launched in India on August 15 to check basic facilities in government schools with student protests that began in Créteil, France, and spread across Europe. The protests concern crowded classrooms, teacher shortages, school buildings, education costs and school spending. The article discusses common themes in students' concerns.

title: UNICEF, stakeholders seek end to child marriage
blurb: UNICEF and stakeholders in Gombe and Bauchi states in Nigeria called for urgent, coordinated action to end child marriage, protect girls' rights and guarantee equal access to education, including for girls with disabilities. The call was made at a stakeholders' engagement organised by UNICEF's Bauchi field office.

title: Quality education begins with the teacher
blurb: This opinion piece discusses how quality education depends not only on policies, classrooms and technology but also on well-supported teachers who can nurture learners, adapt to change and improve learning outcomes. It highlights the central role of teachers in everyday school life.

title: AI-powered scams raise stakes of student data breaches, cybersecurity expert warns
blurb: A cybersecurity expert says EdTech platforms handling student data can face risks through third-party services such as payment gateways and cloud providers. He suggests stronger security checks on each integration to protect children's information.

title: School heads seek law to protect educational institutions, teachers from violence
blurb: School heads are asking for a law to protect educational institutions and teachers from violence. The item reflects a request from school leaders for stronger legal safeguards for the school community.

title: School choice improves learning at a lower cost, analysts say
blurb: Supporters of school choice programmes in the United States argue that giving families more options can improve student outcomes at lower cost. The article notes that more than 30 states have some form of school choice programme and that 30 states have opted into a federal tax credit programme taking effect on January 1, 2027.

title: EDUTHON 6.0 BRINGS 1,200+ EDUCATION LEADERS TO CHANDIGARH TO DISCUSS AI AND THE FUTURE OF SCHOOL EDUCATION
blurb: Eduthon 6.0 in Chandigarh brought together more than 1,200 education leaders to discuss artificial intelligence and the future of school education.

title: Union education minister urges students to focus on innovation to build developed India
blurb: Union Minister Prahlad Joshi, speaking in Patna, said education should go beyond rote learning and urged students to focus on innovation for a developed India by 2047. He said NEP 2020 promotes critical thinking and creativity. The Seva Sankalp Abhiyan competitions involved students from 95,195 schools across 38 districts in Bihar.

title: Education Minister ‘worried’ about reading skills as Luxembourg lags in Pisa test
blurb: Luxembourg's Education Minister has said he is concerned about reading skills after the country's results in the PISA test. The item points to attention on literacy outcomes in an international assessment. No further detail was provided in the source summary.

blurb: The Ministry of Education has conducted a nationwide screening on inclusive education through the PRASHAST portal.
